facts.statement: Anserimimus fossils were discovered in the Bayankhongor province of Mongolia during a Soviet-Mongolian expedition in the late 1970s.
facts.quote: Anserimimus was found in the Mongolian aimag, or province, of Bayankhongor during a joint Soviet-Mongolian expedition to the Gobi Desert, in the late 1970s.

facts.statement: The genus Anserimimus was named by Mongolian paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold in 1988.
facts.quote: Mongolian paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold named Anserimimus in 1988

facts.statement: The only known species of Anserimimus is Anserimimus planinychus.
facts.quote: The one named species of Anserimimus is called Anserimimus planinychus.

facts.statement: There is only one known specimen of Anserimimus, the holotype IGM 100/300.
facts.quote: There is only a single specimen of Anserimimus, its holotype IGM 100/300.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton is rather complete and articulated but lacks the skull and lower jaws.
facts.quote: It consists of a rather complete and articulated skeleton lacking the skull and lower jaws.

facts.statement: Anserimimus lived during the early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: The layer Anserimimus was found, is dated from the early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, or about 70 million years ago.

facts.statement: Anserimimus fossils were recovered from the Nemegt Formation in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Anserimimus was recovered from the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.

facts.statement: The Nemegt Formation environment consisted of alluvial plains with meandering rivers, mudflats, and shallow lakes.
facts.quote: The Nemegt is thought to represent alluvial plains containing meandering rivers.

facts.statement: Anserimimus was a lanky, fast-running animal that was possibly an omnivore.
facts.quote: It was a lanky, fast-running animal, possibly an omnivore.

facts.statement: Anserimimus closely resembled other ornithomimids but had more powerful forelimbs.
facts.quote: From what fossils are known, it probably closely resembled other ornithomimids, except for its more powerful forelimbs.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Anserimimus to be 3 meters long and weigh 50 kilograms in 2010.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul in 2010 estimated its length at 3 m, and its weight at 50 kg.

facts.statement: Other studies suggested the holotype of Anserimimus could have weighed between 143.6 and 170 kilograms.
facts.quote: Other studies suggested that the holotype was heavier, weighing up to 143.6 - 170 kg.

facts.statement: The thighbone (femur) of Anserimimus is 435 millimeters long.
facts.quote: The thighbone is 435 millimetres long.

facts.statement: Anserimimus had long, nearly straight claws on its hands with a nearly flat lower surface.
facts.quote: The claws on the hand are long, low at the back, and rather straight, only slightly curved, with the lower surface nearly flat.

facts.statement: Anserimimus had a long, powerful forelimb with large crests on the shoulder and upper arm bone that attached large muscles like the biceps.
facts.quote: The forelimb is long and also built more powerfully than that of other ornithomimids, with large crests on the scapulocoracoid of the shoulder and humerus (upper arm bone), which provided attachment points for large arm muscles like the biceps.

facts.statement: The metacarpus of Anserimimus's hand was fused, adding to the limb's strength.
facts.quote: The metacarpus of the hand is fused, adding to the strength.

facts.statement: The function of Anserimimus's powerful arm with straightened claws remains unknown.
facts.quote: The function of the powerful arm, with its straightened claws, remains unknown.

facts.statement: The unique arm structure may indicate a different food-gathering strategy than other ornithomimids, but the diet is difficult to determine because the skull is unknown.
facts.quote: It may indicate a different diet of food-gathering strategy than other ornithomimids, although its diet is difficult to determine, since the animal's skull is unknown.

facts.statement: It is debated whether ornithomimids like Anserimimus were omnivores or herbivores despite descending from carnivorous ancestors.
facts.quote: Scientists have long hypothesized that ornithomimids, descended from carnivorous theropod ancestors, were actually omnivores or even herbivores.

facts.statement: Anserimimus was assigned to the family Ornithomimidae, a group of derived Ornithomimosauria.
facts.quote: Anserimimus was by Barsbold assigned to the Ornithomimidae, a group of derived Ornithomimosauria.

facts.statement: Gallimimus from the same formation is considered a possible closest relative of Anserimimus.
facts.quote: Its closest relative may be Gallimimus from the same formation albeit from a different area (Kobayashi & Lu, 2003; Kobayashi & Barsbold, 2005).

facts.statement: Some studies have been unable to specifically determine the relationships of Anserimimus or other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Other studies have been unable specifically to determine its relationships or those of any other ornithomimids (Ji et al., 2003; Makovicky et al., 2004).

facts.statement: Anserimimus was discovered in Bayanhongor Province, Mongolia, during a Soviet-Mongolian expedition to the Gobi Desert in the late 1970s.
facts.quote: Anserimimus fue encontrado en la provincia o aymag de Bayanhongor, Mongolia durante una expedición soviético-mongola al Desierto de Gobi, a finales de los años 1970.

facts.statement: The Mongolian paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold named Anserimimus in 1988.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo mongol Rinchen Barsbold nombró a Anserimimus en 1988

facts.statement: Only one species, A. planinychus, is known, named for its distinctive flat claws.
facts.quote: Solo se conoce una especie de Anserimimus llamada A. planinychus, del latín planus que significa plano, del griego onychos por garra, en referencia a la peculiares garras planas que identifican al género.

facts.statement: There is only one known specimen of Anserimimus, the holotype IGM 100/300 found in the Nemegt Formation.
facts.quote: Sólo hay un solo espécimen de Anserimimus, su holotipo IGM 100/300 encontrado en la formación Nemegt.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a fairly complete and articulated skeleton that lacks the skull and lower jaw.
facts.quote: Se compone de un esqueleto bastante completo y articulado que carece de cráneo y la mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: Robert Bronowicz provided a detailed description of the species in an unpublished 2005 thesis, referencing additional material including a second partial skeleton, ZPAL MGD-I / 65.
facts.quote: En una tesis inédita Robert Bronowicz en 2005 dio una descripción detallada de la especie, refiriéndose también material adicional a la misma, entre las que un segundo esqueleto parcial, la muestra de ZPAL MGD-I / 65.

facts.statement: In 2010, Bronowicz concluded that the second specimen, though closely related to A. planinychus, likely represents a separate taxon.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 2010 Bronowicz concluyó este otro espécimen, aunque estrechamente relacionados con A. planinychus, probablemente representa un taxón separado.

facts.statement: Barsbold classified Anserimimus as a member of the family Ornithomimidae, a group of ornithomimosaurian derivatives.
facts.quote: Barsbold asignó a Anserimimus como un miembro de la familia Ornithomimidae, un grupo de derivados ornitomimosaurianos.

facts.statement: Modern cladistic analysis has confirmed Anserimimus as a close relative of Gallimimus.
facts.quote: Esto ha sido confirmado por la moderna análisis cladístico siendo un cercano relativo de Gallimimus.

facts.statement: However, other studies have been unable to specifically determine its relationships with Gallimimus or any other ornithomimid.
facts.quote: Sin embargo otros estudios han sido incapaces específicamente de determinar sus relaciones con este o los de cualquier otro ornitomímido.

facts.statement: The Nemegt terrain was a floodplain with meandering rivers dating to the Maastrichtian, approximately 74 to 65 million years ago.
facts.quote: El terreno de Nemegt representa una llanura inundable con ríos meandrosos, datada durante el Mastrichtiano hace aproximadamente 74 a 65 millones de años.

facts.statement: Anserimimus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sediments indicate a rich habitat offering abundant diverse food sources that could support massive Cretaceous dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Los sedimentos también indican que existía un hábitat rico, ofreciendo diversos alimentos en cantidades abundantes que podrían sostener los masivos dinosaurios cretácicos.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the second partial skeleton specimen represents a separate taxon distinct from A. planinychus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 2010 Bronowicz concluyó este otro espécimen, aunque estrechamente relacionados con A. planinychus, probablemente representa un taxón separado.

rejected.statement: Anserimimus had a strongly arctometatarsalian foot where the third metatarsal was excluded from the front surface of the metatarsus for over 40% of its upper length.
rejected.quote: The foot is strongly arctometatarsalian, with the third metatarsal excluded from the front surface of the metatarsus over 40% of its upper length.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'excluded from the front surface of the metatarsus'
